newsitem.title: USA: Chase Q2 net up 11 pct before merger costs.
newsitem.headline: Chase Q2 net up 11 pct before merger costs.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp, the largest U.S. bank based on asssets, said Tuesday its operating net income rose 11 percent in the second quarter, before merger related restructuring costs, reflecting strength in its wholesale and consumer businesses.

"These excellent-second quarter results demonstrate Chase's vibrant wholesale and consumer business franchises, and the benefits of our customer-focused execution," chairman and chief executive Walter Shipley said in a statement.
Chase Manhattan's second-quarter operating net income was $969 million, compared to $870 million a year ago.
Fully diluted earnings per share, before the merger-related restructuring costs, rose to $2.11 per share from $1.82, an increase of 16 percent.
During the period, the company spent $630 million to buy back its common shares. Common shares outstanding at the end of the quarter totaled 423.3 million versus 437.1 million a year ago.

Chase Manhattan said higher revenues in its regional and nationwide consumer banking businesses were offset by an increase in loan losses and expenses related to marketing initiatives and new product offerings, leading to a decline in operating net income to $330 million from $346 million a year ago.

In credit cards, net income declined, reflecting higher credit card charge-offs and expenses related to co-branding initiatives. Credit card net income was $39 million in the second-quarter of 1997, down from $81 million a year ago.
